ranking_fidelity_gate.description: MASS-session ranking recipe rebuilt verbatim from the committed script; all three committed AXIS=MASS masks recomputed and compared before any PRUNE mask was built. NOT bit-identical: after the IR-DEC-07 sentinel fix in ensure_unpacked_bands the agreement is <=50 px symmetric difference per arm (observed values in 'arms'), i.e. <=12 boundary dots at each ranking cut, attributed to float-path differences between the MASS session's environment and this one (this environment is run-to-run deterministic). With the previously committed raw-band unpack the disagreement was 602-2,246 px per arm and H33-A was a constant surface (holdout AUC 0.5000).

variants.form_note: h33-h33-2-b2; PRUNE dcat>3px refill to 37654 (swap 2171 ring dots); pred +0.001 to +0.007
variants.predicted_change: +0.001 to +0.007 DTI (MODEL: swap 2,171 misregistration-halo ring dots for top-ranked >3 px ridge dots at fixed count)

mechanism_card.hypothesis: R0's 2,171 dots at 2.24-3.00 px (224-300 m) from a catalogue trace are mostly off-position re-detections of the catalogue faults themselves, not unmapped splays. Replacing them with the top-ranked corroborated ridge dots lying >3 px (>300 m) from every catalogue pixel, at unchanged count 37,654, increases live DTI.
mechanism_card.mechanism: GeoDAWN Area 2 was flown at ~400 m line spacing, so lineament positions are uncertain by about the 300 m kernel radius (https://data.usgs.gov/datacatalog/data/USGS:657e1d85d34e23d3533209f7): a ridge detected within ~300 m of a mapped trace is most parsimoniously that same fault, misregistered. The organizers mask known pixels pixel-exactly and score neighbouring pixels against new-fault truth only (https://community.drivendata.org/t/scoring-clarification-are-known-usgs-ingenious-faults-masked-when-scoring-and-are-they-in-the-final-round-label-set/11516), so a re-detection dot's kernel credit falls on masked pixels that are not in the test truth set: it pays the alpha-weighted false-positive cost and earns ~nothing. The parent's lineage already tightened this collar twice (44,090 dots 0.2600 CLAIM -> d_cat>1 40,199 dots 0.2708 CLAIM -> d_cat>2 37,654 dots 0.2778 CLAIM) but cut mass each time, so the collar effect was never isolated; this arm extends the collar to the kernel radius at fixed mass, refilling by the parent's own exact-marginal-gain ranking.
mechanism_card.non_fault_mimic: Two confounders. (1) The signal being removed could be real: unmapped parallel splays, relay strands or fault-zone widening within 300 m of a mapped trace count as new fault per the organizers (https://community.drivendata.org/t/where-do-you-draw-the-line/11536). (2) The refill targets could be non-faults: lithologic contacts, dike-swarm magnetic lineaments or strandline terraces >300 m from mapped faults (the same mimic class as the MASS +10% arm).
mechanism_card.predicted_sign_and_size: Positive: +0.001 to +0.007 DTI (MODEL). Decomposition: the confounded d_cat>1 -> d_cat>2 step gained +0.0070 CLAIM while also removing 2,545 dots of mass; attributing roughly half of that to the collar gives ~+0.003 for removing 2,171 comparable ring dots, plus a refill value near break-even (the MASS +10% arm's marginal dots are predicted -0.003..+0.0025). The parent ranking q itself values near-catalogue dots highly (its ridge fields respond to the known faults), so q-based gain sums understate the case for tightening; only a live receipt adjudicates. Per brief section 5, a live change under 0.01 on the public chunks is no evidence either way.
mechanism_card.falsifier: A receipt at or below 0.2678 (R0 CLAIM 0.2778 minus the 0.01 no-evidence band) falsifies the misregistration-halo hypothesis and proves the (2,3] px ring carries real unmapped test splays worth more than the best >3 px refill dots. A receipt at or above 0.2878 supports it. Between the two: no evidence on public chunks; do not spend another collar slot until a MASS receipt fixes the parent mass.

variants.form_note: h33-h33-2-b2; PRUNE dcat>1px rank-trim to 37654 (2492 ring dots in); pred -0.007 to +0.001
variants.predicted_change: -0.007 to +0.001 DTI (MODEL: re-admit (1,2] px ring dots, rank-trimmed to 37,654; bracketing arm for the collar curve)

mechanism_card.hypothesis: Loosening the collar from >2 px to >1 px -- re-admitting the 2,545 lineage dots at 141-200 m from catalogue traces and dropping the same number of lowest-ranked dots elsewhere to hold 37,654 -- decreases live DTI if those ring dots are misregistered re-detections of mapped faults, and increases it if they are unmapped near-trace splays.
mechanism_card.mechanism: This is the historical 0.2708 CLAIM emission's collar (measured identity: solo == d2_8 & (d_cat > 1)) rebuilt at R0's mass. The 0.2708 -> 0.2778 step mixed collar tightening with a 6.3% mass cut; holding the count at 37,654 by the parent's exact-marginal-gain ranking isolates the collar. Together with R0 (d_cat>2) and the d_cat>3 arm, the three receipts would trace the fixed-mass collar response curve. Note the ranking q is structurally favourable to ring dots (its inputs respond to the known faults themselves), so the trim retains the ring dots q likes most -- the strongest form of the loose-collar case this lineage can make.
mechanism_card.non_fault_mimic: The ring dots' topographic/geophysical ridges can be produced by the mapped fault's own scarp, damage-zone fracturing or juxtaposed-lithology contact offset by survey misregistration -- signal that is real geology but is the catalogue fault, whose pixels are masked out of the test truth. Alluvial fan-head trenching along the range front produces the same 100-200 m offset lineaments without any fault.
mechanism_card.predicted_sign_and_size: Negative: -0.007 to +0.001 DTI (MODEL) -- the reverse of the lineage's d_cat>1 -> d_cat>2 gain, net of the mass effect that this arm removes. This is a bracketing/diagnostic arm, not a score-maximising one; SLOT_PLAN holds it conditional on the d_cat>3 receipt being inconclusive.
mechanism_card.falsifier: A receipt at or above 0.2878 (R0 CLAIM + 0.01) falsifies the misregistration-halo model of the near-catalogue ring and would redirect the campaign toward near-trace splay hunting. At or below 0.2678 it corroborates the model. Between: no evidence on public chunks.

report_only_diagnostics.note: REPORT ONLY (never gates). The catalogue hide-and-recover holdout correlated -0.87..+0.54 with live scores historically (brief section 3).
report_only_diagnostics.sgmc_structural_bias_note: SGMC truth is defined beyond a 3 px catalogue dilation, so by construction no SGMC truth pixel can reward the (1,2] px ring dots that prune_dcat_gt1 adds or punish prune_dcat_gt3 for removing (2,3] px dots. For this axis the SGMC control is biased in favour of the tighter collar; it is reported for comparability with the MASS session and must not be used to rank the two PRUNE arms.
